subject: Nanotechnology
title: Colloidal Self-Assembly
description: A micro-lesson that makes Colloidal Self-Assembly usable.

hook.text: Opals shimmer because silica spheres self-assembled into a crystal lattice — their color comes from structure, not pigment.

buildup.text: Colloidal nanoparticles in solution can organize into crystals, chains, or clusters depending on their interactions.

discovery.text: DNA-coated colloids assemble into specific crystal structures — sequence determines which particles bond to which.

twist.text: Defect-free colloidal crystals are hard to grow — gravity, sedimentation, and kinetic traps create imperfections.

climax.text: Colloidal photonic crystals now serve as structural-color inks, sensors, and optical coatings without any dyes.

punchline.text: An opal is nature's proof that particles can build crystals on their own.

quiz.question: Why do opals display iridescent colors?
options: They contain colored pigment molecules between layers
Self-assembled silica spheres form a crystal lattice that diffracts light, creating structural color
Chemical impurities absorb specific wavelengths of light
